gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: "We are leaving now." — They said they ___ then.
'We're leaving here at dawn,' they said. They said they were leaving ___ at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Place adverbs shift with the speaker's perspective: here → there.

gaps.sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
gaps.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm meeting them tomorrow evening,' she said. She said she was meeting them ___ evening.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow evening becomes the next (or the following) evening.

gaps.sentence: The colonel ___ his soldiers to advance at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Order + object + to-infinitive reports a command; suggest and hope do not take object + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'No, I won't open the door,' he said. He ___ to open the door.
gaps.explanation: Refusals are reported with refuse + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.
